who: Your father. Your father. Your father.
Both of you. We are waking both of you.
We're waking him. We're waking him up.
how: How did I come? How did I come?
Under the road. It's dry under the road.
On my feet. Same as you.
gift: Nothing. Nothing at all. Open the door.

innocent_answers.clean_boots: Got a lift on a cart most of the way, thanks be to God.
innocent_answers.dry: Came under the big umbrella. Not a drop on me.
innocent_answers.dog_growl: That dog never liked me. Never.

answers.who: Your father, Patrick. Who else would it be.
answers.how: Across the bog road. On foot.
answers.gift: Nothing. I came to sit with him.

answers.who: Your father, child. And mind the clocks stay stopped for the both— for him. For him.
answers.how: Walked, the way my mother walked to every wake.
answers.gift: Salt and a clay pipe for the table, as is right.

answers.who: Paddy Donnelly. We were boys together on that very road. The same road that took... ah, never mind an old man.
answers.how: Slowly, with the stick. The road's longer than it was.
answers.gift: A story or two. He'd want them told.

answers.who: Your poor father. God rest him, Ronan.
answers.how: Down the lane. I'm soaked through.
answers.gift: A candle for the window, and some soda bread.

answers.who: Patrick Donnelly.
answers.how: Through the woods. Your dog will smell the hare on me, pay him no mind.
answers.gift: A brace of rabbits for the widow.

answers.who: Donnelly. Owed me two shillings, God rest him anyway.
answers.how: On my two bad legs, how else?
answers.gift: Myself, and be grateful.

answers.who: Patrick... and— yes. Patrick.
answers.how: The long way, by the lake. I like to watch the water.
answers.gift: Flowers from the ditch. They're a bit wet.

answers.who: Old Patrick! Mam says the bog took him. And she says I'm not to say the rest.
answers.how: Ran the whole way, look at the state of my boots.
answers.gift: Bread from Mam. And I'm to tell her everything.

answers.who: Your father. ...You don't know, do you?
answers.how: I walked.
answers.gift: A prayer. It's all I have left to give.

answers.who: Is it a wake? I thought it was a wedding! ...Patrick, yes. Patrick.
answers.how: I followed the singing. There was no singing. I got lost twice.
answers.gift: Ale! Well. Half the ale.

answers.who: Patrick, God love him. He knew every verse.
answers.how: Singing up the road to keep the dark off.
answers.gift: A song for him, and a bottle for us.

answers.who: Donnelly. The tenant on the lower field.
answers.how: In the trap, of course. I'll not walk the bog like a labourer.
answers.gift: My presence. And a good word with the priest.

answers.who: Y-your father. Mister Donnelly, I mean.
answers.how: I ran. There's something in the hedges tonight, I swear it.
answers.gift: Mam's rosary. She said to put it in your hands. Not his. Yours.

answers.who: Your father, Ronan. Are the mirrors covered? All of them?
answers.how: By the chapel road. It's the only safe one at night.
answers.gift: Holy water, blessed this morning.

answers.who: Your father. I built his coffin today. And the other one.
answers.how: Cut through the yard behind the forge.
answers.gift: Nails for the lid, when it's time.

answers.who: Patrick. And the one who went into the water after him.
answers.how: Around the fairy fort, never through it.
answers.gift: Rowan berries. Keep them by the door.

answers.who: Paddy! Good old Paddy! Is he not coming out to greet us?
answers.how: Stumbled, mostly. The ditch caught me once.
answers.gift: A drop of the good stuff. Mostly full.

answers.who: Your father, Ronan... I worked his fields.
answers.how: Across the fields. The boots are ruined.
answers.gift: Eggs. Sorry. They're a bit broken.

answers.who: Patrick Donnelly, owed me for a lamp. I'll not mention it tonight.
answers.how: On the cart, so I did. Kept my boots out of the muck.
answers.gift: Tobacco and snuff for the table. Free, tonight.

answers.who: Patrick. He'd dance to anything, that man.
answers.how: Under the hedge, minding the fiddle from the rain.
answers.gift: The fiddle. A slow air, if you'll allow it.

nights.name: Seamus
nights.line: Evening. I came as soon as I heard. God rest him.

nights.name: Bridget
nights.line: Let me in, child. The rain is in my bones.

nights.name: Sultan
nights.line: Is there ale? Grand. I'll sing him a song, so I will!

nights.name: Old Tom
nights.line: I knew him forty years. I'll sit with him tonight.

nights.name: James
nights.line: God bless all here. He loved a good song, didn't he?

nights.name: Daniel
nights.line: S-sorry. Am I too early? Mam said I had to come. She said not to look at you.

nights.name: Nora
nights.line: I've brought a candle for the window. Two, actually. Mam said two.

nights.name: Michael
nights.line: Open up, it's Michael from the crossroads.

nights.name: Sultan
nights.line: Evenin' again! I brought the ale back. Well... most of it.

nights.name: Joseph
nights.line: Are the mirrors covered? Every one of them? Good.

nights.name: Paddy
nights.line: Is there a chair by the fire for an old man?

nights.name: John
nights.line: I made the coffin. Odd thing — they had me measure for two.

nights.name: Eileen
nights.line: Sorry I'm late. The bog road is all water. Same as the night they went in.

nights.name: Martin
nights.line: I brought the fiddle. Just a slow air, mind.

nights.name: Mary Kate
nights.line: It's Mary Kate. Mam sent me over with bread.

nights.name: Peter
nights.line: Evening. Peter, with the cart. I'm the one brought them home from the bog. Both of them.

nights.name: Siobhan
nights.line: Is he laid out in the room? I'll say a prayer for the both of you.

nights.name: Sultan
nights.line: Third night! I know all the songs now, so I do. Shall I sing one for him?

nights.name: Denis
nights.line: Open the door! I've a drop here for the poor man!

nights.name: Jeremiah
nights.line: Did you hear it out on the road? Keening. Two voices tonight.

nights.name: Timothy
nights.line: Evening... I'm from the farm up the hill. God, Ronan. You look just the way they said you would.

nights.name: William
nights.line: Make way. I'll not stand in the rain like a labourer.
